arguments.spec:
# Contradiction hunt in the merged policy brief

`input/brief.md` merges four sources (2024 commerce policy, security review, finance retention memo, live campaign)
that have never been reconciled. Every one of its 20 clauses (C-01..C-20) ends in a machine-readable `[key = value]`
tail; two clauses sharing a key are talking about the same setting -- that normalisation already happened.

- A conflict is exactly two clauses sharing a key with different values: `contradiction` when neither value is
  `unspecified`, `ambiguity` when one is. Two clauses sharing a key with the SAME value are never a conflict, even
  when it is tempting to flag it -- a false conflict is worse than a missed one.
- The deliverable is `spec/conflicts.json`. Every flagged conflict needs a `why` (>=12 chars); once `complete` is
  set to true, every conflict must carry its own resolving `assumption` (>=20 chars).
- `input/`, `test/`, and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are frozen evidence and must never be edited -- the verifier
  re-derives the true conflict set from the brief itself on every `npm test` run.
- Set `complete: true` only on the last card, once every conflict is flagged and every one is resolved, verified by
  two real `npm test` runs (green before AND after the flip) -- the same shape as the prior project's finalize card.

## Derived ground truth (read from the frozen brief and verifier directly; do not re-derive from scratch)

20 clauses, 14 distinct keys. Only 5 keys are shared by more than one clause, producing exactly 6 conflicting pairs:

| Key | Clauses (value) | Pairs | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipping.free_threshold_minor | C-02 (4900), C-09 (4900), C-14 (2500) | C-02+C-14, C-09+C-14 | contradiction (C-02+C-09 is NOT a conflict -- same value) |
| refund.auto_approve.max_minor | C-04 (5000), C-11 (0) | C-04+C-11 | contradiction |
| data.retention_days | C-12 (90), C-18 (400) | C-12+C-18 | contradiction |
| password.min_length | C-06 (12), C-19 (unspecified) | C-06+C-19 | ambiguity |
| session.idle_timeout | C-07 (15m), C-16 (unspecified) | C-07+C-16 | ambiguity |

The other 9 keys (page.p95_latency_ms, subscription.max_active, email.confirmation_delay_s, search.paid_placement,
giftcard.max_splits, basket.abandon_after, stock.max_staleness, dsar.response_days, price.vat_included) are each
carried by exactly one clause and produce no pairs at all.
arguments.plan:
# Plan: sequential key-by-key contradiction resolution

All six cards after the first write to the single shared file `spec/conflicts.json`, so they are chained
STRICTLY SEQUENTIALLY (each `dependsOn` the previous) rather than run in parallel -- there is no safe fan-out when
every card touches the same file.

1. **index-clauses-and-resolve-shipping-conflict** -- the only card that must read the whole brief before acting,
   because a shared key can sit clauses apart; it produces the full clause index and, since it already has the
   full picture, resolves the one key shared by three clauses (shipping.free_threshold_minor).
2. **resolve-refund-approval-conflict** -- refund.auto_approve.max_minor (C-04 vs C-11).
3. **resolve-retention-window-conflict** -- data.retention_days (C-12 vs C-18).
4. **resolve-password-policy-ambiguity** -- password.min_length (C-06 vs C-19).
5. **resolve-session-timeout-ambiguity** -- session.idle_timeout (C-07 vs C-16).
6. **finalize-contradiction-hunt** -- the completeness pass: confirm all six conflicts are flagged and resolved,
   flip `complete` to true, and prove it with two real `npm test` runs (before and after), exactly mirroring how
   the previous spec-api-design-consistency project's finalize-completeness card closed that project out.

Each conflict card writes both the conflict AND its assumption in the same turn -- the brief's own guidance is that
the reasoning for which side wins is sitting in the prose you just read, and is much harder to reconstruct later.
